outcomes: An agent can inspect a fresh worktree before its first build without manually creating the workspace index
Independent preparation work overlaps without duplicate index publication or nondeterministic results
Installation has a compact live view and leaves only completed actions and actionable diagnostics in the terminal
nonGoals: Running dependency installers, Cloud setup, or context generation from an MCP read
Changing extension pins or parsing language manifests in core to synthesize an index
Parallelizing hooks or writes whose independence has not been established
Hiding errors or interpreting arbitrary extension log text as proof of a filesystem change

requirements.text: MCP prepares a missing index through the shared probe within a bounded deadline, without full installation, and reloads an index replaced after its first read. Concurrent preparation serializes publication, bounds and reports lock waiting, and rechecks freshness after acquiring ownership. An inaccessible lock warns and permits an in-memory view without publication; cancellation never bypasses an active lock. MCP preparation failure remains actionable and retryable.

Independent stale provider probes execute with bounded concurrency. Their results and diagnostics are merged in stable provider order and the validated index is published once only after the required probes succeed.

Independent extension and template artifacts restore with bounded concurrency while lock updates and result reporting are committed in stable order after workers finish. An install writes the lock only when a requested fact changed, never for a same-version platform digest or download source alone. Hooks retain their existing sequencing and a failure never publishes a successful install marker.

Default installation renders preparation progress in place on a supported terminal and prints a concise completed-action summary without unchanged artifact checks or successful job transcripts. Verbose mode exposes details, failures retain diagnostics, and redirected or machine output never receives terminal control sequences or human text on the machine stdout stream.
